title: spells._release ends the holding Concentration before _take_effect validates the release, so a refused release (for example, target out of range) loses the held spell and isn't a clean refusal. Check the release (targets, range, affected targets) before calling end_concentration so a Refusal leaves the spell held, and drop the dissipate-on-refusal branch in combat._readied_triggers.

problems: review: rejected (I'm rejecting this. Pulling the cast-time target checks into a shared _check_targets is sound, and calling it before end_concentration fixes the out-of-range, Total Cover and sight cases. The tests use the real cast(ready=True) path and check the right behaviour. The ticket isn't fully solved, though. A ready cast never runs the spell handler, so the handler's own Refusals fire for the first time at release, after Concentration has ended. Spare the Dying on a target that's been healed, a mismatched Magic Missile dart split, and a bad Command word or Lesser Restoration condition all do this. The diff also removes the combat guard that dropped the held spell in exactly that case. Now those paths put a held spell back in readied with no Concentration behind it.)

review: other dungdra/spells.py:240 _release now runs _check_targets before end_concentration, but spell handlers can still raise Refusal after Concentration has ended. A ready=True cast never runs the handler, so the handler's own checks run for the first time at release. For example, _spare_the_dying (line 1019) refuses a target that isn't at 0 HP, which can change between cast and release. _magic_missile (1281/1287) refuses a dart split that doesn't match, _command (1144) refuses a bad word and _lesser_restoration (1436) a bad condition. Each of these raises after end_concentration, so the release still loses the held spell and isn't a clean refusal. The ticket asks that a refused release leave the spell held, and that isn't true yet for these paths.

review: other dungdra/combat.py:838 The dissipate-on-refusal branch is gone, but a refusal raised after end_concentration can still happen (see the spells.py finding). In that case the except branch puts rec back in cb.readied even though rec.held is no longer the readier's Concentration. A later trigger could then release a spell with no Concentration holding it, which breaks GLOSS.ready#9. Removing the branch is only safe once every refusal happens before Concentration ends: run the handler's option and target validation before end_concentration (or move that validation into the release check), or keep the guard.
